title: Family buying for own stay
opening: Hi, saw your Pearl Residences post. Looking for own stay with family. Can share more?
persona: Married couple with two school-age children. Both commute around Seberang Jaya. They like the idea of facilities but worry about whether 900 sqft works. They do not volunteer all of this at once.
motives: Practical family routine, enough usable space, commute, manageable ongoing costs.
facts: Own-stay; spouse and two children; currently renting; uncertain about bedroom fit; moderate interest.

title: First-time buyer unsure of priorities
opening: Hi, first time buying. Not sure what I should look at first tbh.
persona: A 29-year-old first-time buyer, living with a sibling for now. Unsure about own stay versus investment and intimidated by the process. Engages when the agent helps prioritize without interrogating.
motives: Understand first decision steps, monthly affordability, avoid choosing blindly.
facts: First purchase; has not set a budget; likely own-stay in 1-2 years; cautious about financing.

title: Budget constraints and price concern
opening: Hi, how much is the 3 bedroom? My budget quite tight, below RM400k if possible.
persona: Young couple with strict budget and no confirmed loan eligibility. Wants price clarity and may ask about rebates or monthly payments. Becomes skeptical if pushed toward a viewing before affordability is addressed.
motives: Stay under budget, know what is verified, avoid surprise costs.
facts: Budget target under RM400k; first home; spouse helps decide; no loan preapproval; exact unit-level current price unknown to the agent.

title: Investor asking about rental return
opening: Hi, considering for investment. What rental yield can expect around there?
persona: Small property investor comparing several northern Malaysian projects. Wants actual rental demand and yield data, not generic claims. Will share that they already own one unit if asked naturally.
motives: Evidence for rental demand, downside risks, compare investment with alternatives.
facts: Existing investor; target net yield above 4%; understands yield depends on price and rents; project-specific yields are not verified.

title: Layout requirement and mismatch
opening: Hi. Need 4 bedrooms for my parents and kids. Your unit got 4 room?
persona: Three-generation household. Four separate bedrooms are non-negotiable because parents need privacy. They may test whether the agent will honestly say the product only offers a three-bedroom standard unit.
motives: Separate rooms and privacy; unwilling to compromise on 4 bedrooms.
facts: Requires four bedrooms; project standard unit is 900 sqft with 3 bedrooms; hard mismatch; not convertible.

title: Location and commuting
opening: Hi, is this convenient for going to work? I work around Prai, wife near Sunway Carnival.
persona: Couple evaluating daily commute and errands. Wants realistic location context, not made-up travel minutes. One works in Prai and the other near Sunway Carnival. They have not said whether they drive.
facts: Own stay; two working adults; both commute; exact travel time and traffic are not verified.

title: Safety, flood and infrastructure concerns
opening: I saw the location near river and power lines. Flood risk or safety concern ah?
persona: Cautious buyer who saw online discussion about river flooding and nearby high-tension infrastructure. Needs honest separation between documented facts and unknown technical assessment. Does not accept blanket reassurance.
facts: No project-specific flood/safety conclusion is verified in the supplied Knowledge. Do not accept reassurance without evidence.

title: Cold and hesitant customer
opening: Hi. Just browsing only, not planning anything yet.
persona: Low-intent browser with little time. Short replies, does not want a sequence of qualification questions. May share one practical interest if the agent gives space and a concise overview.
motives: Browse privately, maybe understand what type of homes this is.
facts: Low intent; no timeline or budget; dislikes pressure; not convertible during this conversation.

title: Changing requirement and returning question
opening: Hi, can tell me about the layout? Need a room for work from home.
persona: Buyer who initially mentions a home office, then changes priority to care for an elderly parent. Later returns to an unanswered question about whether maintenance fee includes clubhouse use. Reacts badly if the agent repeats room count instead of tracking the changed need.
motives: Adaptable work space; support parent; clarify actual ownership costs and pay-per-use details.
facts: Own stay; needs flexible room; parent may stay over; maintenance fee and clubhouse charge are separate considerations; do not assume all costs are verified.

title: High intent, sensitive to pressure
opening: Hi, I may want to see the show unit this weekend. But don't want agent keep chasing me after ya.
persona: High-intent couple ready to consider a viewing, but sensitive to sales pressure and repeated follow-up. Wants a low-pressure visit and asks whether the time can be confirmed. No live appointment calendar is provided.
motives: See actual layout, retain control, no repeated follow-up, no false booking confirmation.
facts: High interest; wants to view this weekend; exact available slots are unknown; only a human can confirm operational booking.

title: Facilities and ownership costs
opening: Hi, how much is the maintenance fee and is the clubhouse included?
persona: An ordinary own-stay buyer comparing monthly ownership costs. Wants to understand the verified maintenance rate, whether clubhouse use is extra, and may discuss a spouse's preference for pool access. Appreciates a clear answer without a feature dump.
motives: Predictable monthly expenses and useful facilities without surprise charges.
facts: No current unit-level price is verified. The knowledge distinguishes maintenance charge and pay-per-use clubhouse. Interest depends on clarity, not generic enthusiasm.

title: Flexible space and family privacy
opening: Hi, I prefer 4 rooms because I work from home and my mum sometimes stays. Do you have that?
persona: Buyer says four rooms initially but uses one as a workspace and the visiting parent stays occasionally. Can reasonably consider a three-bedroom layout if the actual room use and privacy work, but does not accept invented floor plans or a partition promise.
motives: Quiet work space and occasional family privacy, with some flexibility in room count.
facts: Initial four-room preference is flexible; verified standard unit has three bedrooms; actual fit requires discussion and probably a real viewing.
